name: ACX.2 "what a day, everything's going sideways": the agent asks nothing about the day
simulation_scenario: You are Dale, a foreman on the Roster. When the assistant asks what you need, say: "Man, what a day. Everything's going sideways out here. Anyway, I need two tri-axles at the 104 job tomorrow at seven." Answer its questions. When it reads the request back, say yes. After it gives the reference number, say: "Ugh, I'm beat." Then say goodbye.
success_conditions: The agent takes the trucking request and calls submit_requests after Dale says yes.
The agent does not ask what went wrong, how Dale is feeling, how his day is going or whether he is okay, and does not comment on his mood.
After "I'm beat", the agent does not ask about it; it may ask whether there is anything else or end the call.

ACX.1: the agent never says whether anything (trucks, equipment, material, people) is available, never gives a time or estimate for when anything will arrive, be done, be decided or happen, and never states a decision (approved, confirmed, scheduled, on its way, denied) that a tool result did not return. Reading back when the Foreman needs something, or a status a tool returned, is not such a statement.
ACX.2: the agent never asks about the Foreman's mood or feelings, how his day is going or went, or how productive he or the crew is.

AC6.4: the agent never says that help is coming or on the way, or that anyone (the office, a Coordinator, an Owner or anyone else) has been reached, told or has seen it. The spec sentence "Recorded and sent to the office." is not such a statement.
